newsitem.title: USA: Oneita may seek relief from creditors.
newsitem.headline: Oneita may seek relief from creditors.

text.p: Oneita Industries Inc said it may have to seek relief from creditors if it is unable to restructure its debt.
As of June 28, 1997, Oneita was in default and not in compliance with debt repayment obligations, the garment maker said in a statement.

Also, Robert Gintel resigned as chairman of the board on August 8, 1997, Oneita said. Gintel holds $7.5 million of subordinated notes in the company that are currently classified as current liabilities, due to default.

Oneita said its revolving credit agreement and its loan agreement with an institutional lender are presently in default, resulting in more than $60 million of debt being classified as current liabilities.
The company said it will meet with creditors for negotiation of a debt restructuring and addressing the company's strategic plans.
